passage.title: Hands
paras: what she has forgotten: how to knead,
how to fold the edges of a samosa
into three neat corners, quick as prayer.
She calls me by my mother's name.
I pass the flour, and her fingers
find the old road home without her.
passage.byline: An unseen poem written for TGA

questions.q: Explore how the poet presents memory in 'Hands'.
questions.a: AO2 points: the paradox of hands remembering; the kitchen list (knead, fold); 'quick as prayer'; the turn at 'She calls me by my mother's name.'; the speaker's restraint ('I do not correct her'); the metaphor 'the old road home'; the final 'without her'; two stanzas moving from skill to loss.

Annotations: name confusion shows memory loss; 'I do not correct her' (gentle love); 'the old road home' metaphor (habit leading back to the past); 'without her' (her mind absent while her hands work).
